title: Russian
description: Everyday Russian in Cyrillic with transliteration: greetings, family, food, numbers, travel and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
units.tip: 'Привет' (privet) is informal; 'здравствуйте' (zdravstvuyte) is the polite hello.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
units.tip: Russian has no 'a' or 'the', and 'is' is usually left out: 'Он мой друг' = He (is) my friend.

units.title: Food and drink
units.tip: 'Я хочу есть' (ya khochu yest', I want to eat) is the usual way to say you are hungry.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
units.tip: After 2, 3 and 4 a noun takes a special form: 'четыре яблока' (chetyre yabloka, four apples).

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
units.tip: 'Налево' / 'направо' mean to the left / right; 'слева' / 'справа' mean on the left / right.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
units.tip: 'Утром' (utrom) means in the morning and 'ночью' (noch'yu) means at night.

exercises.prompt: I drink coffee in the morning.
